name: Silkworm
label: Touch and Go
lede: Three friends from Missoula, a drummer from Seattle and an engineer from their old high school: twenty years of records critics loved and crowds mostly missed, ended by a stranger's car at a Skokie stoplight.

eras.title: Ein Heit in Missoula
eras.text: Silkworm began as teenagers in Missoula, Montana, a long way from any music industry. The band that later made eight albums started as Ein Heit and a couple of self-dubbed cassettes.

years.h: Tim Midyett, Andy Cohen and Joel Phelps start Ein Heit
years.p: In Missoula, Montana, the three future Silkworm songwriters play together as Ein Heit, which lasts until June 1987.

years.h: Silkworm forms in Missoula
years.p: Silkworm officially starts in November 1987. Tim Midyett, away at college, joins in June 1988.

years.h: Advantage, the first Silkworm demo tape
years.p: Silkworm self-release the Advantage cassette in 1988 and Girl Harbrr in 1989, before moving the band to Seattle.

eras.title: Seattle, where nobody came
eras.text: They moved to Seattle just as the whole world was about to look there, and still couldn't draw a crowd. What they found instead was a drummer, Michael Dahlquist, and a producer from their own high school.

q: We simply didn't know any better!
years.h: Silkworm move to Seattle; Michael Dahlquist joins on drums
years.p: Silkworm arrive in Seattle in early 1990 and add drummer Michael Dahlquist, who grew up in nearby Bothell. For years they play sparsely attended local shows and do better in Chicago, New York and San Francisco.
years.xp: Tim Midyett's own history of the band puts their persistence down to naivety: they kept booking shows because they didn't know any better.

years.h: L'ajre, Silkworm's first album
years.p: Silkworm's debut album comes out on the small label Temporary Freedom, after a run of 7-inch singles starting in 1991.

years.h: In the West: Steve Albini, a fellow Hellgate High grad
years.p: While Silkworm are on Northwestern's WNUR, [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] calls in, and they learn he went to Hellgate High School in Missoula too. He produces In the West for C/Z Records, the start of a long partnership.

q: I just really didn't want to have to make any choices.
years.h: Joel RL Phelps quits Silkworm just before Libertine
years.p: Joel Phelps leaves in 1994, citing his health and the strain of touring. Tim Midyett wrote that the band found it easy to carry on as a trio.
years.xp: Phelps later told Vice the exit was driven by his mental health and a touring schedule he couldn't sustain. He described years of alcohol abuse that turned into full addiction before he got sober, and later volunteered in addiction recovery.

years.h: Libertine, the last album with Joel Phelps
years.p: Released on El Recordo after Joel Phelps had already quit, Libertine was reissued as a 2×12-inch with bonus tracks by Comedy Minus One in May 2014.

eras.title: A trio on Matador
eras.text: Cut down to three, Silkworm signed to Matador and finally got onto real tours. Albini kept recording them, now in Seattle and at his own house.

years.h: Firewater: first trio album, and a Matador deal
years.p: Silkworm's Firewater, on Matador, puts them on the road with [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]] and [[Guided by Voices|6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb]]. Comedy Minus One announced an expanded 2xLP reissue for December 4, 2026.

years.h: Developer, recorded by Albini in Seattle and at his house
years.p: Steve Albini records Silkworm's Developer at Robert Lang Studios in Seattle and at his home. The 2025 reissue adds a [[Bob Dylan|72c536dc-7137-4477-a521-567eeb840fa8]] cover with [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] of [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]].

eras.title: Touch and Go lifers
eras.text: From 1998 Silkworm made four albums for Touch and Go: praised, steady, never a hit. Bedhead's Matt Kadane joined them on keyboards on later records.

years.h: Blueblood, Silkworm's Touch and Go debut
years.p: Silkworm move to Touch and Go with Blueblood. Matador rounds up the early singles the same year as Even a Blind Chicken Finds a Kernel of Corn Now and Then: 1990–1994.

years.h: The Crust Brothers: Silkworm plus Stephen Malkmus
years.p: Michael Dahlquist and Silkworm play covers with [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] as The Crust Brothers, released in 1998 as the live album Marquee Mark.

years.h: Lifestyle, the second Touch and Go album
years.p: Silkworm's Lifestyle arrives in 2000, the middle of the band's four-album run on Touch and Go.

years.h: Italian Platinum, with Bedhead's Matt Kadane on keys
years.p: [[Matt Kadane|7449c305-8a29-46e1-8934-ced2f4f7e6ef]] of Bedhead adds keyboards to Silkworm's Italian Platinum. The You Are Dignified EP follows on 12XU in 2003.

years.h: It'll Be Cool, Silkworm's last album
years.p: It'll Be Cool is the final Silkworm album with Michael Dahlquist, and the band's last on Touch and Go.

eras.title: A red light on Dempster Street
eras.text: A woman trying to kill herself drove into the car carrying Michael Dahlquist and two other Chicago musicians. It ended Silkworm, and the court case took three more years.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jeanette Sliwinski · Touch and Go Records
years.h: Michael Dahlquist is killed in a crash in Skokie, Illinois
years.p: At a red light on Dempster Street, Jeanette Sliwinski drove her Mustang at high speed into the car carrying Silkworm drummer Michael Dahlquist, 39, and musicians Douglas Meis and John Glick. All three died.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Sliwinski had argued with her mother and was trying to kill herself; she had been hospitalized for psychiatric care two weeks earlier. She was arrested in her hospital room the next day and charged with three counts of first-degree murder.

Meis played in the Dials and EXO, Glick in the Returnables. Touch and Go posted a memorial to Dahlquist on July 18, 2005.

years.h: Chokes! EP, and Bottomless Pit rises from Silkworm
years.p: 12XU releases Silkworm's Chokes! EP. Tim Midyett and Andy Cohen go on as [[Bottomless Pit|b427ea89-6351-4e61-8f76-74d7b7ecf295]], which runs until an indefinite hiatus in 2014.

years.h: Jeanette Sliwinski convicted of reckless homicide, not murder
years.p: Pleading not guilty by reason of insanity, Jeanette Sliwinski is acquitted of first-degree murder in the Skokie crash and convicted of reckless homicide. She is sentenced to eight years and paroled October 2, 2008.

eras.title: Couldn't you wait?
eras.text: A documentary made the case for Silkworm to people who'd missed them. Then Steve Albini's death brought the surviving three back on stage, with Joel Phelps singing for the first time since 1994.

years.cap: Couldn't You Wait? The Story of Silkworm
years.h: Couldn't You Wait? The Story of Silkworm premieres
years.p: The documentary on Silkworm features interviews with [[Jeff Tweedy|63287966-6021-474a-ba76-edc37a5f1b7c]], [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] and [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]].

years.h: Steve Albini dies of a heart attack at 61
years.p: Steve Albini, who recorded Silkworm from In the West on and shared their Missoula high school, dies of a heart attack at his Chicago home.

years.h: Silkworm reunite for Steve Albini, Joel Phelps back after 30 years
years.p: Silkworm play a tribute concert for Steve Albini, Joel Phelps's first show with the band since 1994. Jeff Panall of [[Songs: Ohia|1305bd7e-27ef-4236-ae87-0a7d435234ca]] and Mint Mile takes Michael Dahlquist's place.

years.h: Developer reissued; Silkworm announce more shows
years.p: Comedy Minus One reissues Developer as an expanded 2xLP limited to 1,000 copies. Pitchfork reports Silkworm will reunite for more shows in 2025.

years.h: Silkworm's first tour since the band ended in 2005
years.p: The reunited Silkworm, with Joel Phelps and Jeff Panall, begin their first tour since Michael Dahlquist's death.
